discovery: Invention of photonic crystal fibres and the control of light guidance by wavelength-scale microstructure

nominees.name: Philip St. J. Russell
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, Erlangen, Germany

motivation: Russell conceived the photonic crystal fibre, and with Knight and Birks he realised it in 1996 by stacking and drawing silica capillaries. Their fibres introduced new physics to optical guidance: endlessly single-mode propagation, engineered dispersion and, in 1999, true photonic-bandgap guidance of light in a hollow air core. This simple, elegant fabrication gave precise control over how light is confined at the wavelength scale. It turned a laboratory curiosity into a global platform. Supercontinuum 'white-light' sources built on these fibres were essential to the frequency-comb metrology recognised in 2005, and they are now standard tools in microscopy and spectroscopy. Hollow-core fibres opened gas-based nonlinear optics and ultrafast pulse compression, and they now carry record-low-loss telecommunications. The same group's work on tapered fibres helped lay the foundation of optical nanofibres. Few inventions in optics have so broadly joined fundamental physics, instrumentation and applications.
